top_news.title: Karnataka may borrow funds to provide drought relief to farmers if needed: Dy CM Parameshwara
top_news.summary: Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara on Thursday said the state government was prepared to borrow funds, if necessary, to provide relief to farmers affected by the worsening drought, as 217 of the state's 240 taluks have been declared drought-hit. Parameshwara said protecting farmers was the government's first priority and that the state would take all possible measures to assist them. He was speaking to the media after visiting and inspecting farmland at Gunnal village in Yelburga taluk. "During recent inspections of drought conditions in Vijayapura and Ballari districts, it was found that 98% of crops in Vijayanagara district had been destroyed. Even the remaining two per cent is unlikely to reach farmers as a viable harvest. The State is facing an extremely difficult situation," Parameshwara said. He said the drought situation in several North Karnataka districts, including Ballari, Vijayanagara, Koppal, Raichur and Vijayapura, was more severe than in the Mysuru region. Parameshwara said the government was prioritising drinking water supply, assistance to farmers and generation of wage employment as part of drought management. He said drought had also triggered migration from villages, citing a Lambani Tanda where residents were on the verge of leaving in search of work. Officials were instructed to provide employment under the rural employment guarantee scheme, he said. "If work is available within rural areas, migration can be prevented. We can survive only if farmers survive. Without farmers, neither society nor Government can sustain itself," he said. Under the norms of the Union government's National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), farmers are to receive a total relief amount of Rs 8,500, comprising the Central and State shares. Parameshwara said the Centre had not yet released its share, prompting the state government to provide Rs 2,500 each from its own share as the first instalment. Around 50 lakh farmers across Karnataka are to receive the assistance, with the government having already spent Rs 1,250 crore for the first instalment. "We acknowledge that this amount is not sufficient to address the distress faced by farmers. But when assistance has to be provided to 50 lakh farmers, the overall expenditure involved must also be considered. Releasing the first instalment is part of the Government's responsibility," he said. The state has submitted to the Centre an assessment of around Rs 46,000 crore in crop losses based on damage in 177 taluks. Parameshwara said Karnataka had sought around Rs 10,000 crore to Rs 12,000 crore in relief from the Centre based on the current assessment and NDRF guidelines. The Union government has sent three teams to Karnataka to assess the drought situation, and relief is expected to be released based on their reports, he said. Parameshwara said a delegation comprising the Chief Minister, the Deputy Chief Minister and Opposition leaders had been planned to meet the Centre and seek drought relief. However, BJP and JD(S) leaders had indicated that they would not participate in the delegation, he said. He said the final loss assessment could increase further and that if losses reached around Rs 60,000 crore by the time the final memorandum was submitted, the state could seek around Rs 18,000 crore to Rs 20,000 crore in relief. "We will have to see how much assistance the Centre ultimately provides. MPs from Karnataka should put pressure on the Centre irrespective of party affiliation. This is not the time for politics; this is the time to stand with farmers," he said. The Deputy Chief Minister also said steps were being taken to ensure that crop insurance payments reached farmers who had lost their crops due to drought. He said the government was also working on measures concerning the share of crop insurance premiums paid by farmers and would seek to ensure that eligible beneficiaries received compensation without delay. Parameshwara said groundwater levels had fallen sharply in several parts of the state, with some areas reporting no water even after drilling to a depth of 500 feet. "In my own region, there are places where even drilling to a depth of 1,800 feet has failed to yield water," he said. He said measures had also been initiated to provide drought-affected farmers with a five-year period for loan repayment. A 60-month moratorium had been provided on loan repayment, during which farmers would not have to repay their loans, he said. The government had also informed banks that it would address related liabilities, including the issue of interest on loans, he added. Farmers were also receiving support through diesel subsidy, electricity subsidy and the government's Guarantee schemes, he said. "If the assistance currently being provided is found to be insufficient, further measures will be taken. Under no circumstances will we abandon farmers. If necessary, the Government is prepared even to borrow money to provide relief. Protecting farmers' livelihoods is the Government's responsibility," he said. Parameshwara said maize farmers in several North Karnataka districts were facing difficulties due to low prices and reduced yields, and that the Union government would be requested to take steps to address the issue. He also said the Centre had a responsibility in determining the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for crops and should provide necessary support on the issue. Responding to a question about reports of some state transport depots running out of diesel and bus services being disrupted over pending payments, Parameshwara said the issue could be temporary and would be rectified immediately. He rejected allegations that the Guarantee schemes had created a financial crisis in the state. "If the Guarantees had caused such a financial problem, the Government could have stopped at least one of the schemes. But we have spent around Rs 52,000 crore on the Guarantee schemes over the past three years and continue to implement them," he said. Parameshwara said the Karnataka government was functioning with fiscal discipline and that the allegation that the Guarantee schemes alone had caused the state's financial difficulties was not correct. Despite the drought, the government would continue to provide assistance to farmers through crop-loss compensation, crop insurance, extension of the loan repayment period, support relating to interest payments and other measures, he said. "The Union Government too must discharge its responsibility in addressing farmers' distress. The State Government has already released the first instalment of relief. In the coming days, efforts will be made to obtain assistance from the Centre and provide further relief to farmers. During drought management, farmers' livelihoods must take precedence over politics," Parameshwara said. (ANI)

top_news.title: Union Jal Shakti Minister Paatil chairs 20th Meeting of Empowered Task Force on Ganga Rejuvenation
top_news.summary: Strengthening the Government's commitment towards holistic river rejuvenation, the 20th Meeting of the Empowered Task Force (ETF) was held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of the Union Minister for Jal Shakti, CR Paatil. According to the Ministry, the meeting reviewed the progress of the Namami Gange Programme and deliberated on key interventions aimed at accelerating river rejuvenation through improved sewage infrastructure, scientific water management, safe reuse of treated wastewater, ecological restoration, groundwater management, nature-based solutions and enhanced coordination among stakeholders. The meeting was also joined by MoS Jal Shakti, Raj Bhushan Chaudhary, along with key stakeholders from various ministries and state governments, including Secretary, Department of Water Resources, Smt. Archana Varma; Secretary, Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ashok K.K. Meena; Director General of the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG), Rajeev Kumar Mital; JS&FA Department of Water Resources, Gaurav Masaldan; and senior officers of NMCG and participating states. The meeting reviewed the status of sewage infrastructure, DPR preparation and appraisal, land availability, Safe Reuse of Treated Wastewater (SRTW), aquifer mapping, wetlands, City Sanitation Action Plans (CSAP), aerial drainage mapping and regular meetings of State Ganga Committees. It was informed that the revised DPR for the Barauni Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) has been received and sent to IIT-BHU for appraisal, while the DPR for Shantipur STPs in West Bengal has been approved by the Executive Committee. Bihar and West Bengal have notified their policies on the reuse of treated wastewater, while Jharkhand is in the process of obtaining State Cabinet approval. The meeting reviewed the overall status of projects under the Namami Gange Programme and the programme's performance during FY 2025-26. As of August 2026, 527 projects have been sanctioned at a total cost of 43,266 crore, of which 368 projects have been completed. Under sewerage infrastructure, 219 projects have been sanctioned, creating a treatment capacity of 6,603 MLD along with a sewer network of 5,245 km. Of these, 147 projects have been completed, creating 4,339 MLD of sewage treatment capacity and completing 4,615 km of sewer network. The Namami Gange Programme also embraces interventions relating to bioremediation and innovative sewage treatment, solid waste management, industrial effluent treatment, surveillance and monitoring, research and development, biodiversity and afforestation, livelihood generation, public outreach and knowledge management. The Minister emphasised the need to maintain the pace of implementation and directed the concerned agencies and State Governments to ensure timely completion of ongoing projects and expeditious action on pending DPRs, land-related issues and other implementation bottlenecks. The meeting also reviewed the academic courses developed under the River City Alliance, in line with the direction to develop water-related courses and facilitate the inclusion of Water Governance and Management in higher education curricula. NMCG and NIUA have developed and facilitated two courses - Principles of Urban River Management and Eco-friendly Waterfront Development. The first course is being offered at Mitraj Sarvajanik, formerly known as SCET Surat, and OP Jindal Global University, while the second is being offered at the School of Planning and Architecture, Bhopal. The courses cover areas including watersheds, drainage basins, river morphology, stormwater management, environmental flows, eco-friendly riverfront design, basin-city connections, floodplain regulation, riparian ecology, water-sensitive urban design and climate resilience. One of the main focuses of the meeting was the rejuvenation of Gomti Udgam Sthal in Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh. The Master Plan for Rejuvenation and Integrated Development of Gomti Udgam Sthal was approved in the 68th Executive Committee meeting of NMCG held in December 2025. In the meeting it was informed that the DPR pertaining to lake restoration and sewage treatment through a 1 MLD Nature-Based Solutions-based STP has been approved, with Administrative Approval and Expenditure Sanction issued on 17 September 2026. The DPR relating to the restoration of turtle habitat and Panchvatika is being considered in the 74th Executive Committee, while the DPR relating to infrastructure development is under examination. The Minister advised that implementation of the approved interventions be initiated without delay and emphasized the need for timely completion of the bidding process and constitution of the State-level Steering Committee. The meeting also reviewed the proposed rejuvenation of the Niranjana/Falgu River in Bihar, with interventions aimed at improving the river ecosystem and enhancing water availability through measures including afforestation, groundwater recharge and recharge trenches. Following a letter issued to the Chief Secretary, Government of Bihar, the Secretary, Water Resources Department, Bihar, has been nominated as the State-level Nodal Officer for the Niranjana rejuvenation initiative. The State-level Nodal Officer has been requested by NMCG to examine and confirm the Bill of Quantities (BOQ) and detailed cost estimates in consultation with all concerned State Departments, including verification of quantities, items and rates as per the latest applicable Schedule of Rates (SOR). The State has been requested to furnish the confirmation at the earliest to facilitate further approval and grounding of the project. C. R. Paatil emphasized the importance of adopting an integrated approach to river rejuvenation, combining ecological restoration with groundwater management and measures aimed at enhancing water availability. The meeting also reviewed the status of NMCG-related interventions for rejuvenation of the River Yamuna. In Uttar Pradesh, NMCG has sanctioned projects in Mathura-Vrindavan, Kosi-Chhata, Agra, Firozabad and Etawah, aimed at strengthening sewage collection, conveyance, treatment and management infrastructure and reducing the discharge of untreated or inadequately treated sewage into the Yamuna and its associated watercourses. In Delhi, apart from wastewater management interventions, others include the constitution of the Yamuna Ecological Task Force, wetland-related interventions, preparation of the Urban River Management Plan for Delhi, drone-based surveys of drains, Nature-Based Solutions, monitoring of pollution-related flows, Grossly Polluting Industries and the Interceptor Sewerage Project, besides augmentation of environmental flows in River Yamuna through the Coronation Pillar and Okhla STPs. The Minister emphasised that such academic initiatives can contribute to building a strong knowledge base and a cadre of professionals equipped to address the ecological, social, cultural, economic and policy dimensions of river management. It was also noted that the courses may be promoted at the city and State levels for river professionals and students, and students undertaking these courses may be considered for river-related assignments in cities. The meeting also reviewed key outreach and public participation initiatives undertaken since the 19th ETF meeting. Under Swachhta Hi Seva 2026, cleanliness drives, awareness campaigns and community engagement activities were undertaken across various locations. The Union Minister of Jal Shakti also interacted with water conservation and river rejuvenation warriors from across the country, recognising their grassroots efforts towards water conservation, environmental protection, river rejuvenation and community mobilisation. The Minister appreciated the contribution of these grassroots champions and emphasised that sustained and focused public participation is essential for translating river rejuvenation efforts into long-term and community-led action. The meeting further reviewed the National level Consultation Workshops on the Framework for Small River Rejuvenation, organised in New Delhi, Pune and Guwahati during July and August 2026, focusing on scientific planning, Nature-Based Solutions, groundwater recharge, environmental flows and community participation. The workshops sought to strengthen a systematic and scientific approach towards the rejuvenation of small rivers and watercourses, while incorporating local ecological conditions and community knowledge. During the 9th India International Water Week 2026, the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework and the Protocol for Riverine Microplastics Monitoring were also launched/released to strengthen sustainable river-city management and scientific monitoring of river pollution. The initiatives are aimed at supporting cities and river authorities in adopting sustainable approaches to urban river management and strengthening scientific monitoring of emerging pollution challenges, including riverine microplastics. On World River Day, the 39th Ganga Task Force of 137 CETF BN (TA) conducted awareness campaigns and cleanliness drives at key riverfront locations in Prayagraj, Varanasi, Kanpur, Lucknow and Delhi, further strengthening public participation in river conservation. The 20th meeting of the Empowered Task Force reiterated the importance of sustained coordination among Central Ministries, State Governments, Urban Local Bodies, scientific institutions and local communities for achieving the objectives of river rejuvenation. Paatil emphasised that river rejuvenation requires a holistic approach that goes beyond pollution abatement to encompass water availability, ecological health, groundwater security, biodiversity conservation, sustainable urban development and community participation. He called for continued coordination and close monitoring at all levels to ensure that interventions translate into measurable outcomes on the ground. The 20th meeting of the Empowered Task Force reiterated that sustained and coordinated efforts across the Ganga Basin will remain central to strengthening the vision of Aviral & Nirmal Ganga, while advancing long-term water security, ecological resilience and sustainable development across the river basin. (ANI)

Together, visitors, exhibitors, speakers and industry delegations represented more than 50 countries. The event covered electronic components, embedded technologies, printed circuit boards, electronic manufacturing services, production machinery, automation, testing, inspection and related manufacturing solutions. articles.title: Karnataka may borrow funds to provide drought relief to farmers if needed: Dy CM Parameshwara
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara on Thursday said the state government was prepared to borrow funds, if necessary, to provide relief to farmers affected by the worsening drought, as 217 of the state's 240 taluks have been declared drought-hit. Parameshwara said protecting farmers was the government's first priority and that the state would take all possible measures to assist them. He was speaking to the media after visiting and inspecting farmland at Gunnal village in Yelburga taluk. "During recent inspections of drought conditions in Vijayapura and Ballari districts, it was found that 98% of crops in Vijayanagara district had been destroyed. Even the remaining two per cent is unlikely to reach farmers as a viable harvest. The State is facing an extremely difficult situation," Parameshwara said. He said the drought situation in several North Karnataka districts, including Ballari, Vijayanagara, Koppal, Raichur and Vijayapura, was more severe than in the Mysuru region. Parameshwara said the government was prioritising drinking water supply, assistance to farmers and generation of wage employment as part of drought management. He said drought had also triggered migration from villages, citing a Lambani Tanda where residents were on the verge of leaving in search of work. Officials were instructed to provide employment under the rural employment guarantee scheme, he said. "If work is available within rural areas, migration can be prevented. We can survive only if farmers survive. Without farmers, neither society nor Government can sustain itself," he said. Under the norms of the Union government's National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), farmers are to receive a total relief amount of Rs 8,500, comprising the Central and State shares. Parameshwara said the Centre had not yet released its share, prompting the state government to provide Rs 2,500 each from its own share as the first instalment. Around 50 lakh farmers across Karnataka are to receive the assistance, with the government having already spent Rs 1,250 crore for the first instalment. "We acknowledge that this amount is not sufficient to address the distress faced by farmers. But when assistance has to be provided to 50 lakh farmers, the overall expenditure involved must also be considered. Releasing the first instalment is part of the Government's responsibility," he said. The state has submitted to the Centre an assessment of around Rs 46,000 crore in crop losses based on damage in 177 taluks. Parameshwara said Karnataka had sought around Rs 10,000 crore to Rs 12,000 crore in relief from the Centre based on the current assessment and NDRF guidelines. The Union government has sent three teams to Karnataka to assess the drought situation, and relief is expected to be released based on their reports, he said. Parameshwara said a delegation comprising the Chief Minister, the Deputy Chief Minister and Opposition leaders had been planned to meet the Centre and seek drought relief. However, BJP and JD(S) leaders had indicated that they would not participate in the delegation, he said. He said the final loss assessment could increase further and that if losses reached around Rs 60,000 crore by the time the final memorandum was submitted, the state could seek around Rs 18,000 crore to Rs 20,000 crore in relief. "We will have to see how much assistance the Centre ultimately provides. MPs from Karnataka should put pressure on the Centre irrespective of party affiliation. This is not the time for politics; this is the time to stand with farmers," he said. The Deputy Chief Minister also said steps were being taken to ensure that crop insurance payments reached farmers who had lost their crops due to drought. He said the government was also working on measures concerning the share of crop insurance premiums paid by farmers and would seek to ensure that eligible beneficiaries received compensation without delay. Parameshwara said groundwater levels had fallen sharply in several parts of the state, with some areas reporting no water even after drilling to a depth of 500 feet. "In my own region, there are places where even drilling to a depth of 1,800 feet has failed to yield water," he said. He said measures had also been initiated to provide drought-affected farmers with a five-year period for loan repayment. A 60-month moratorium had been provided on loan repayment, during which farmers would not have to repay their loans, he said. The government had also informed banks that it would address related liabilities, including the issue of interest on loans, he added. Farmers were also receiving support through diesel subsidy, electricity subsidy and the government's Guarantee schemes, he said. "If the assistance currently being provided is found to be insufficient, further measures will be taken. Under no circumstances will we abandon farmers. If necessary, the Government is prepared even to borrow money to provide relief. Protecting farmers' livelihoods is the Government's responsibility," he said. Parameshwara said maize farmers in several North Karnataka districts were facing difficulties due to low prices and reduced yields, and that the Union government would be requested to take steps to address the issue. He also said the Centre had a responsibility in determining the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for crops and should provide necessary support on the issue. Responding to a question about reports of some state transport depots running out of diesel and bus services being disrupted over pending payments, Parameshwara said the issue could be temporary and would be rectified immediately. He rejected allegations that the Guarantee schemes had created a financial crisis in the state. "If the Guarantees had caused such a financial problem, the Government could have stopped at least one of the schemes. But we have spent around Rs 52,000 crore on the Guarantee schemes over the past three years and continue to implement them," he said. Parameshwara said the Karnataka government was functioning with fiscal discipline and that the allegation that the Guarantee schemes alone had caused the state's financial difficulties was not correct. Despite the drought, the government would continue to provide assistance to farmers through crop-loss compensation, crop insurance, extension of the loan repayment period, support relating to interest payments and other measures, he said. "The Union Government too must discharge its responsibility in addressing farmers' distress. The State Government has already released the first instalment of relief. In the coming days, efforts will be made to obtain assistance from the Centre and provide further relief to farmers. During drought management, farmers' livelihoods must take precedence over politics," Parameshwara said. (ANI)

articles.title: Union Jal Shakti Minister Paatil chairs 20th Meeting of Empowered Task Force on Ganga Rejuvenation
articles.summary: Strengthening the Government's commitment towards holistic river rejuvenation, the 20th Meeting of the Empowered Task Force (ETF) was held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of the Union Minister for Jal Shakti, CR Paatil. According to the Ministry, the meeting reviewed the progress of the Namami Gange Programme and deliberated on key interventions aimed at accelerating river rejuvenation through improved sewage infrastructure, scientific water management, safe reuse of treated wastewater, ecological restoration, groundwater management, nature-based solutions and enhanced coordination among stakeholders. The meeting was also joined by MoS Jal Shakti, Raj Bhushan Chaudhary, along with key stakeholders from various ministries and state governments, including Secretary, Department of Water Resources, Smt. Archana Varma; Secretary, Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ashok K.K. Meena; Director General of the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG), Rajeev Kumar Mital; JS&FA Department of Water Resources, Gaurav Masaldan; and senior officers of NMCG and participating states. The meeting reviewed the status of sewage infrastructure, DPR preparation and appraisal, land availability, Safe Reuse of Treated Wastewater (SRTW), aquifer mapping, wetlands, City Sanitation Action Plans (CSAP), aerial drainage mapping and regular meetings of State Ganga Committees. It was informed that the revised DPR for the Barauni Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) has been received and sent to IIT-BHU for appraisal, while the DPR for Shantipur STPs in West Bengal has been approved by the Executive Committee. Bihar and West Bengal have notified their policies on the reuse of treated wastewater, while Jharkhand is in the process of obtaining State Cabinet approval. The meeting reviewed the overall status of projects under the Namami Gange Programme and the programme's performance during FY 2025-26. As of August 2026, 527 projects have been sanctioned at a total cost of 43,266 crore, of which 368 projects have been completed. Under sewerage infrastructure, 219 projects have been sanctioned, creating a treatment capacity of 6,603 MLD along with a sewer network of 5,245 km. Of these, 147 projects have been completed, creating 4,339 MLD of sewage treatment capacity and completing 4,615 km of sewer network. The Namami Gange Programme also embraces interventions relating to bioremediation and innovative sewage treatment, solid waste management, industrial effluent treatment, surveillance and monitoring, research and development, biodiversity and afforestation, livelihood generation, public outreach and knowledge management. The Minister emphasised the need to maintain the pace of implementation and directed the concerned agencies and State Governments to ensure timely completion of ongoing projects and expeditious action on pending DPRs, land-related issues and other implementation bottlenecks. The meeting also reviewed the academic courses developed under the River City Alliance, in line with the direction to develop water-related courses and facilitate the inclusion of Water Governance and Management in higher education curricula. NMCG and NIUA have developed and facilitated two courses - Principles of Urban River Management and Eco-friendly Waterfront Development. The first course is being offered at Mitraj Sarvajanik, formerly known as SCET Surat, and OP Jindal Global University, while the second is being offered at the School of Planning and Architecture, Bhopal. The courses cover areas including watersheds, drainage basins, river morphology, stormwater management, environmental flows, eco-friendly riverfront design, basin-city connections, floodplain regulation, riparian ecology, water-sensitive urban design and climate resilience. One of the main focuses of the meeting was the rejuvenation of Gomti Udgam Sthal in Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh. The Master Plan for Rejuvenation and Integrated Development of Gomti Udgam Sthal was approved in the 68th Executive Committee meeting of NMCG held in December 2025. In the meeting it was informed that the DPR pertaining to lake restoration and sewage treatment through a 1 MLD Nature-Based Solutions-based STP has been approved, with Administrative Approval and Expenditure Sanction issued on 17 September 2026. The DPR relating to the restoration of turtle habitat and Panchvatika is being considered in the 74th Executive Committee, while the DPR relating to infrastructure development is under examination. The Minister advised that implementation of the approved interventions be initiated without delay and emphasized the need for timely completion of the bidding process and constitution of the State-level Steering Committee. The meeting also reviewed the proposed rejuvenation of the Niranjana/Falgu River in Bihar, with interventions aimed at improving the river ecosystem and enhancing water availability through measures including afforestation, groundwater recharge and recharge trenches. Following a letter issued to the Chief Secretary, Government of Bihar, the Secretary, Water Resources Department, Bihar, has been nominated as the State-level Nodal Officer for the Niranjana rejuvenation initiative. The State-level Nodal Officer has been requested by NMCG to examine and confirm the Bill of Quantities (BOQ) and detailed cost estimates in consultation with all concerned State Departments, including verification of quantities, items and rates as per the latest applicable Schedule of Rates (SOR). The State has been requested to furnish the confirmation at the earliest to facilitate further approval and grounding of the project. C. R. Paatil emphasized the importance of adopting an integrated approach to river rejuvenation, combining ecological restoration with groundwater management and measures aimed at enhancing water availability. The meeting also reviewed the status of NMCG-related interventions for rejuvenation of the River Yamuna. In Uttar Pradesh, NMCG has sanctioned projects in Mathura-Vrindavan, Kosi-Chhata, Agra, Firozabad and Etawah, aimed at strengthening sewage collection, conveyance, treatment and management infrastructure and reducing the discharge of untreated or inadequately treated sewage into the Yamuna and its associated watercourses. In Delhi, apart from wastewater management interventions, others include the constitution of the Yamuna Ecological Task Force, wetland-related interventions, preparation of the Urban River Management Plan for Delhi, drone-based surveys of drains, Nature-Based Solutions, monitoring of pollution-related flows, Grossly Polluting Industries and the Interceptor Sewerage Project, besides augmentation of environmental flows in River Yamuna through the Coronation Pillar and Okhla STPs. The Minister emphasised that such academic initiatives can contribute to building a strong knowledge base and a cadre of professionals equipped to address the ecological, social, cultural, economic and policy dimensions of river management. It was also noted that the courses may be promoted at the city and State levels for river professionals and students, and students undertaking these courses may be considered for river-related assignments in cities. The meeting also reviewed key outreach and public participation initiatives undertaken since the 19th ETF meeting. Under Swachhta Hi Seva 2026, cleanliness drives, awareness campaigns and community engagement activities were undertaken across various locations. The Union Minister of Jal Shakti also interacted with water conservation and river rejuvenation warriors from across the country, recognising their grassroots efforts towards water conservation, environmental protection, river rejuvenation and community mobilisation. The Minister appreciated the contribution of these grassroots champions and emphasised that sustained and focused public participation is essential for translating river rejuvenation efforts into long-term and community-led action. The meeting further reviewed the National level Consultation Workshops on the Framework for Small River Rejuvenation, organised in New Delhi, Pune and Guwahati during July and August 2026, focusing on scientific planning, Nature-Based Solutions, groundwater recharge, environmental flows and community participation. The workshops sought to strengthen a systematic and scientific approach towards the rejuvenation of small rivers and watercourses, while incorporating local ecological conditions and community knowledge. During the 9th India International Water Week 2026, the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework and the Protocol for Riverine Microplastics Monitoring were also launched/released to strengthen sustainable river-city management and scientific monitoring of river pollution. The initiatives are aimed at supporting cities and river authorities in adopting sustainable approaches to urban river management and strengthening scientific monitoring of emerging pollution challenges, including riverine microplastics. On World River Day, the 39th Ganga Task Force of 137 CETF BN (TA) conducted awareness campaigns and cleanliness drives at key riverfront locations in Prayagraj, Varanasi, Kanpur, Lucknow and Delhi, further strengthening public participation in river conservation. The 20th meeting of the Empowered Task Force reiterated the importance of sustained coordination among Central Ministries, State Governments, Urban Local Bodies, scientific institutions and local communities for achieving the objectives of river rejuvenation. Paatil emphasised that river rejuvenation requires a holistic approach that goes beyond pollution abatement to encompass water availability, ecological health, groundwater security, biodiversity conservation, sustainable urban development and community participation. He called for continued coordination and close monitoring at all levels to ensure that interventions translate into measurable outcomes on the ground. The 20th meeting of the Empowered Task Force reiterated that sustained and coordinated efforts across the Ganga Basin will remain central to strengthening the vision of Aviral & Nirmal Ganga, while advancing long-term water security, ecological resilience and sustainable development across the river basin. (ANI)
